sn20.7:1.2: Probably the people known in Sanskrit as the Daśārṇa of the western Vindhya mountains. | The _mudiṅga_ is a doubled-headed drum known today as _mridangam_, which is still widely used in southern India. It is named for the paste (“mud”, today called the _karanai_) applied to one of the heads that gives it its distinctive snare tone (_chapu_). The head is attached with a wooden rim tightened with leather straps. | _Āṇaka_ is another name for what is said to be a large military drum. The context here suggests that the original sense was “plugged”, in reference to the pegs used under the leather straps for tuning, as seen in the modern _mardala_.
sn20.7:1.4: The _pokkhara_ is the drumskin. The _mridangam_ is constructed from a single hollowed-out log, the _phalaka_ (“shell”).
